new_statements.quote: Phonological words in Bahnaric may be mono- or disyllabic, with the latter generally treated as sesquisyllablic (iambic stress). An illustrative example is Smith’s maximum word template for Sedang (1979:22): (CpVp)(Cm)Ci(Cm)V(G)(N)(Cf)(R) [...] The vowels in stressed and unstressed syllables differ in their phonological status. Typically only a single non-contrastive vowel, usually schwa or conditioned variant, and a reduced consonant inventory occur in unstressed syllables, while the main syllables carry the full and rather large range of contrastive vowels and consonants. [...] Like most Austroasiatic languages, the Bahnaric languages are not tonal, but many—such as Sedang—contrast two phonation types
new_statements.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Jennifer Herington & Paul Sidwell. 2013. Bahnaric linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-lxvii. Mahidol University / SIL International. (CC BY)

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Branch-level generalisation in a bibliography's introduction ('Phonological words in Bahnaric.. sesquisyllabic (iambic stress).. the Bahnaric languages are not tonal'), illustrated with Sedang; Takua appears only in the ISO index. Since the claim is main-syllable (final) stress in non-tonal register languages, statement_type is better 'stress' than 'stress-and-tone'. | checker: Cheeseman, Herington & Sidwell 2013, MKS 42 (CC BY). the PDF we hold is not yet in the mirror (held_mirror/source_audit_2026-09-16/taku1254/ is empty), but A's work-dir extract is on and was opened: title page (authors, 'Pages: xxxiv-xlvii', CC licence, ISO list incl. tkz) matc…
new_statements.relation_note: iambic stress on sesquisyllables; non-tonal; North Bahnaric register contrast
new_statements.rule_in_words: Branch-level: Bahnaric words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (reduced presyllable + full main syllable) with iambic, i.e. word-final (main-syllable) stress; the languages are not tonal; most or all North Bahnaric languages (the subgroup containing Takua) have a two-way register (phonation) contrast instead. Nothing is said about Takua individually.
new_statements.exceptions: none for stress; Sedang noted as contrasting creaky vs modal voice rather than breathy vs modal
new_statements.identity_note: Takua [tkz] is explicitly inside the work's scope (ISO code list in the abstract; language index p. lxvii 'Takua 6a tkz'), but the prosodic statement in section 3 is a family-level generalization over Bahnaric, illustrated with Sedang; no Takua data are cited and the bibliography contains no Takua-specific entry at all (Maier 1964 Takua vocabulary is not listed). Treat as branch-level, second-hand.
